description: You are an oncology nurse practitioner specialising in gynaecological oncology at a cancer centre. One of your patients with BRCA1-mutated high-grade serous ovarian cancer has recently been initiated on olaparib (PARP inhibitor) maintenance therapy following platinum-based chemotherapy. The patient has a pre-existing diagnosis of partial epilepsy managed by neurology. The neurology team has sent a referral asking you to advise on the safety of three proposed antiepileptic medication options in the context of the olaparib therapy: carbamazepine (enzyme-inducing antiepileptic, first-line for partial seizures), warfarin (note: this is not an antiepileptic but was included by neurology for anticoagulation co-management of the patient's DVT), and acenocoumarol (similarly included by haematology for anticoagulation). Using the Liverpool Cancer iChart Archive app, look up the interaction rating for each of these three co-medications against olaparib. Then navigate to and remain on the Interaction Details screen specifically for olaparib's interaction with carbamazepine, which is the antiepileptic drug being considered for initiation.

metadata.expected_mechanism: CYP3A4 induction by carbamazepine substantially reduces olaparib AUC
metadata.clinical_context: BRCA1-mutated ovarian cancer patient on olaparib with epilepsy requiring antiepileptic therapy
